school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York

boards.school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Columbia University
boards.description: Morningside Heights transforms after dark, with students moving from Butler Library to local institutions that have fueled late-night study sessions and post-event gatherings for decades.

cards.title: The On-Campus Late Night Hub
cards.subtitle: John Jay Hall Lower Level
cards.notes: Located in the basement of John Jay Hall, this campus staple serves burgers and comfort food until 10:00 AM daily, making it the primary late-night dining hall for students.
cards.short_summary: JJ's Place is Columbia's official late-night dining destination, offering a casual environment for students to use meal swipes for burgers and snacks well into the morning.
cards.evidence_claim: JJ's Place is open from 12:00 PM to 10:00 AM every day and serves as a late-night destination for burgers and specialty sandwiches.
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 10:00 AM. Access requires a Columbia University ID and meal plan swipe or Flex points.

cards.title: The Giant Slice Tradition
cards.subtitle: 2848 Broadway
cards.notes: Famous for its oversized jumbo slices that require two paper plates, this pizzeria stays open until 4:00 AM on weekends to feed the Morningside Heights night crowd.
cards.short_summary: Koronet Pizza is a neighborhood institution known for its massive slices and late-night hours, serving as a reliable stop for students after long library sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Koronet Pizza at 2848 Broadway is open until 4:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays, and until 2:00 AM on other nights.
cards.access_notes: Open until 4:00 AM on Fri-Sat; 2:00 AM Sun-Thu. Counter service with limited indoor seating.

cards.title: The Seinfeld Diner
cards.subtitle: 2880 Broadway
cards.notes: This iconic diner, featured in 'Seinfeld,' offers 24-hour service from Thursday through Sunday morning, providing a classic booth setting for late-night milkshakes and fries.
cards.short_summary: Tom's Restaurant is a historic Morningside Heights diner that serves as a late-night landmark for students, especially during its 24-hour weekend operations.
cards.evidence_claim: Tom's Restaurant is open 24 hours on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, and until 1:30 AM on other nights.
cards.access_notes: 24-hour service available Thursday through Saturday nights. Traditional diner seating.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Grocery Run
cards.subtitle: 2840 Broadway
cards.notes: A 24-hour gourmet grocery store at 110th Street that provides prepared foods, fresh produce, and snacks for students at any hour of the night.
cards.short_summary: Westside Market is a critical 24-hour resource for Columbia students, offering a wide variety of prepared meals and groceries just south of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Westside Market location at 2840 Broadway is open 24 hours daily.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours every day. Includes a large prepared foods section.

cards.title: The Library Fuel Station
cards.subtitle: Butler Library Lobby
cards.notes: Located inside the main campus library, this café serves coffee and snacks until midnight during the week to support students during long study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Blue Java in Butler Library is the essential on-campus coffee stop for students pulling late nights in the university's primary research library.
cards.evidence_claim: Blue Java Butler is open Monday through Thursday until 12:00 AM during the academic term.
cards.source_title: Blue Java Café - Butler Library | Columbia Dining
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight Mon-Thu. Requires Columbia ID for library entry.

cards.title: The Late-Night Sweet Tooth
cards.subtitle: 1030 Amsterdam Ave
cards.notes: Specializing in warm cookies delivered until 3:00 AM, this shop is a go-to for students seeking a sugar boost during late-night group projects or social gatherings.
cards.short_summary: Insomnia Cookies provides late-night bakery items and delivery service to the Columbia community, operating well past midnight every day of the week.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies locations typically serve warm cookies until 1:00 AM or 3:00 AM depending on the day.
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM on weekends and 1:00 AM on weekdays. Delivery and pickup available.

cards.title: The Gourmet Deli Run
cards.subtitle: 2892 Broadway
cards.notes: A family-owned specialty food shop known for its signature sandwiches and imported goods, serving the campus community until 10:00 PM daily.
cards.short_summary: Milano Market is a popular destination for high-quality sandwiches and deli items, frequently visited by students before the late-night study block begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Milano Market Westside at 2892 Broadway is open 7 days a week from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM.
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 10:00 PM. Offers a wide selection of prepared sandwiches and gourmet groceries.

cards.title: The Broadway Slice
cards.subtitle: 2859 Broadway
cards.notes: Located at 111th Street, this pizzeria provides a quick counter-service option for students, with delivery available until 1:00 AM for late-night cravings.
cards.short_summary: Famous Famiglia is a reliable pizza option on Broadway that stays open late for both pickup and delivery to the Morningside Heights area.
cards.evidence_claim: Famous Famiglia Pizzeria at 2859 Broadway offers pickup until 12:00 AM and delivery until 1:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Open for pickup until midnight and delivery until 1:00 AM daily.

cards.title: The Intellectual Late Night
cards.subtitle: 1030 Amsterdam Ave
cards.notes: A legendary windowless café across from St. John the Divine where students write dissertations over bottomless coffee and strudel until 11:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: The Hungarian Pastry Shop is a historic, Wi-Fi-free haven for writers and students, offering a quiet late-night atmosphere for study and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hungarian Pastry Shop is open seven days a week until nearly 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: The Upper West Side's Hungarian Pastry Shop Is Open for Everything
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 11:00 PM. Cash only. No Wi-Fi available.

cards.title: The Midnight Study Space
cards.subtitle: John Jay Hall
cards.notes: During peak academic periods, the main John Jay dining area opens as a no-swipe-required study hall until 10:00 PM, providing extra space for late-night work.
cards.short_summary: The John Jay After-Hours Study Hall is a seasonal university initiative that repurposes dining space for late-night student productivity.
cards.evidence_claim: The main seating area of John Jay opens after hours to all Columbia students (no swipe required) as an additional study space until 10:00 PM during designated periods.
cards.source_title: Events - After-Hours Study Hall | Columbia Dining
cards.access_notes: Available during finals and midterms. Open to all Columbia students without a meal swipe.

boards.school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student spaces and specialized facilities that define daily life at Columbia, from hidden library stacks to rooftop observatories.

cards.title: The Butler Stacks
cards.subtitle: Deep-core study carrels in Butler Library
cards.notes: Enter through the 3rd-floor circulation desk to find these windowless, multi-level carrels. It is the ultimate destination for distraction-free, silent cramming sessions.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level labyrinth of silent study carrels located in the central core of Columbia's main humanities library.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler Library's main collection of 2 million volumes is located in the Stacks, which feature study tables and wireless access throughout.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 during the academic term for CUID holders; accessible via the 3rd-floor entrance.

cards.title: Avery Lower Level
cards.subtitle: Quiet basement study area in Avery Hall
cards.notes: Head to the lower floor for a cozy, ultra-quiet atmosphere surrounded by architectural archives. It is often less crowded than the main reading room upstairs.
cards.short_summary: A serene, subterranean study space within the world-renowned Avery Architectural & Fine Arts Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Avery Library offers quiet study spaces on its lower floor, which are available to all students space-permitting.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM most weeknights; CUID required for entry.

cards.title: Pupin Rooftop Observatory
cards.subtitle: Stargazing dome atop Pupin Hall
cards.notes: Visit on select Friday nights for free public lectures and guided stargazing through the 14-inch telescope. It offers a rare clear view of the sky from Manhattan.
cards.short_summary: A historic rooftop observatory atop Pupin Hall that hosts public stargazing events and astronomy lectures.
cards.evidence_claim: The astronomy department offers free public lectures and guided stargazing at the Rutherfurd Observatory every other Friday during the school year.
cards.access_notes: Public events typically start at 8:00 PM on Fridays; check the outreach calendar for specific dates.

cards.title: Lerner Piano Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student lounge in Alfred J. Lerner Hall
cards.notes: Relax in the 2nd-floor lounge where students often play the Steinway Grand Piano. It's a popular spot for casual socializing between classes.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable central lounge in the student union featuring a grand piano available for student use.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Lounge in Lerner Hall features a Steinway Grand Piano that students are welcome to play.
cards.source_title: Main Lounge | Alfred J. Lerner Hall
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Lerner Hall building hours; open to all CUID holders.

cards.title: St. Paul's Chapel
cards.subtitle: Historic non-denominational chapel
cards.notes: Step inside to experience the incredible acoustics and the Nakashima Peace Altar. It is a designated quiet space for meditation and prayer daily.
cards.short_summary: A landmarked campus chapel known for its Byzantine-style interior and exceptional acoustic properties.
cards.evidence_claim: The chapel is open daily for private meditation and prayer, Monday to Friday, 10am to 5pm.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM for meditation; also hosts evening concerts.

cards.title: NoCo Science Library
cards.subtitle: Modern study space in the Northwest Corner Building
cards.notes: Utilize the floor-to-ceiling windows for a bright study environment. The 400 level allows for collaborative work, while the 600 level is for quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech, light-filled library focusing on STEM fields with designated collaborative and quiet zones.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science & Engineering Library features collaborative spaces on the 400 level and quiet study on the 600 level.
cards.access_notes: CUID required; hours vary by semester but typically open until midnight.

cards.title: Philosophy Hall Lounge
cards.subtitle: GSAS student center in Philosophy Hall
cards.notes: Located in Room 301, this lounge offers a quiet community space for graduate students. It features an acoustic design to minimize background noise.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated social and study hub for graduate students located in the historic Philosophy Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Student Center in 301 Philosophy Hall offers a community space for graduate students to socialize and study.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 8:00 AM to 12:00 midnight; CUID access required.

cards.title: Earl Hall Prayer Space
cards.subtitle: Multi-faith prayer and meditation rooms
cards.notes: Visit Room 110 for a dedicated prayer space with rugs. The building serves as a sanctuary for spiritual well-being and student religious life.
cards.short_summary: A historic building housing multi-faith prayer rooms and the Office of Religious Life.
cards.evidence_claim: Earl Hall Room 110 provides a dedicated prayer space for the Columbia community.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; open to all students for reflection and prayer.

cards.entity_name: Milstein Center for Teaching and Learning
cards.title: Milstein Reading Nooks
cards.subtitle: Modern study alcoves at Barnard College
cards.notes: Look for the signature green swiveling chairs and blue booth-style couches on the 2nd floor. These nooks offer great views and integrated power outlets.
cards.short_summary: Highly sought-after individual study alcoves and modern seating in Barnard's flagship library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Milstein Center features individual desk nooks and booth-style couches on the second floor for focused studying.
cards.access_notes: Open to Columbia and Barnard students; volume decreases as you ascend to higher floors.

cards.title: Gottesman Silent Floor
cards.subtitle: Quiet study at Teachers College
cards.notes: Head to the 3rd floor of Russell Hall for intensive, silent study. The large windows provide scenic views of the surrounding Morningside Heights neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: The designated silent floor of the largest education library in the United States.
cards.evidence_claim: The 3rd floor of the Gottesman Libraries is a designated quiet space for intensive study.
cards.access_notes: Open to TC and Columbia affiliates; check library site for current seasonal hours.

boards.school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Columbia's campus and the surrounding Morningside Heights neighborhood with these social activities and spaces that require no admission or purchase.

cards.title: Lounge on the Low Steps
cards.subtitle: Morningside Campus Centerpiece
cards.notes: Gather on the granite steps for people-watching and sunbathing. This iconic social hub is the primary meeting spot for students between classes.
cards.short_summary: The university's central outdoor social gathering spot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Low Library steps are a natural gathering place for students and a social agora in good weather.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 to CUID holders; public access currently requires guest registration or neighbor QR code.

cards.title: Visit the Wallach Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Lenfest Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Explore contemporary art exhibitions and MFA thesis shows in this sleek Manhattanville space. It is the university's premier public visual arts venue.
cards.short_summary: A free public art gallery showcasing contemporary works.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wallach Art Gallery is free and open to the public Wednesday through Sunday from 12 to 6 PM.
cards.source_title: PLAN YOUR VISIT - Wallach Art Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday-Sunday, 12:00 PM - 6:00 PM. No CUID required for entry.

cards.title: Attend a Sacred Music Concert
cards.subtitle: Historic Campus Chapel
cards.notes: Listen to world-class organists and chamber ensembles in a landmark setting. Concerts are held regularly throughout the academic year.
cards.short_summary: Free professional music performances in a historic landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacred Music presents free concerts at St. Paul's Chapel that are open to the public with advance registration.
cards.access_notes: Concerts typically start at 6:00 PM. Non-affiliates must register by 11:00 AM the day prior.

cards.title: Study in the Butler Stacks
cards.subtitle: Main Humanities Library
cards.notes: Find a quiet carrel or a grand reading room in Columbia's largest library. It is a quintessential campus experience for late-night academic sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus library offering vast study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler Library houses collections in humanities and history and provides numerous service points and study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Open late; CUID required for entry. Visitors require an appointment or temporary pass.

cards.title: Watch the Sunset at Riverside
cards.subtitle: Hudson River Waterfront
cards.notes: Walk two blocks west of campus to enjoy river views and green lawns. The park hosts free yoga and movie screenings during the summer months.
cards.short_summary: A scenic waterfront park perfect for outdoor recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Summer on the Hudson offers over 400 free events including movies and yoga in Riverside Park.
cards.source_title: Summer on the Hudson - Riverside Park Conservancy
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: Relax by the Waterfall
cards.subtitle: 113th Street and Morningside Ave
cards.notes: Visit the pond and waterfall at the base of the cliffs. This peaceful spot is ideal for a nature break just steps from the eastern campus gates.
cards.short_summary: A scenic natural feature in the adjacent community park.
cards.evidence_claim: Morningside Park features a waterfall and pond that host community festivals and jazz concerts.
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: Find Peace in Earl Hall
cards.subtitle: Center for Religious Life
cards.notes: Use the quiet rooms for meditation or prayer. This historic building serves as a sanctuary for students of all faith traditions on campus.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated space for spiritual life and quiet reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Earl Hall provides prayer and meditation spaces and is the home of the University Chaplain.
cards.access_notes: CUID required for campus entry; building accessible via south entrance facing Lewisohn Hall.

cards.title: Explore NYC Museums for Free
cards.subtitle: Student Arts Initiative
cards.notes: Use your CUID to get free admission to over 30 museums, including MoMA and the Met. It is one of the most valuable perks of being a Columbia student.
cards.short_summary: Free access to major NYC cultural institutions for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Passport to Museums program provides current Columbia students free admission to over 30 NYC museums with a valid CUID.
cards.source_title: Museums - Arts Initiative at Columbia University
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid CUID with a current semester validation sticker.

cards.title: Hang Out at The Forum
cards.subtitle: Manhattanville Campus Hub
cards.notes: Enjoy the open, modern ground floor with plenty of seating and free Wi-Fi. This glass-walled space is designed to bridge the university and the community.
cards.short_summary: A modern, transparent community and university gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forum is an open space with glass walls and a clean, modern look available for study and gathering.
cards.source_title: Where to Study at Columbia University - University Life
cards.access_notes: Ground floor is generally open to the public during regular building hours.

cards.title: Stroll Along College Walk
cards.subtitle: 116th Street Pedestrian Path
cards.notes: Walk the brick-paved path between Broadway and Amsterdam. In winter, the trees are famously lit with white lights, creating a festive atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: The central pedestrian thoroughfare of the Morningside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: College Walk connects Broadway and Amsterdam and is the heart of the Morningside campus.
cards.access_notes: CUID required for entry; local neighbors can request access via a specific QR code program.

boards.school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Navigate Columbia's diverse academic landscape with these ten distinct study environments, ranging from silent historic reading rooms to modern collaborative hubs.

cards.title: The Silent Standard
cards.subtitle: Butler Library, Room 301
cards.notes: Find a seat at the long wooden tables in this grand, high-ceilinged room. It is strictly silent, making it ideal for deep focus and long reading sessions.
cards.short_summary: A premier silent study hall located on the third floor of Butler Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lawrence A. Wien Reference Room on the third floor is designated for working in absolute silence.
cards.source_title: Your guide to the Columbia libraries depending on your study needs
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 during the academic term; valid CUID required for entry.

cards.title: The Dark Academia Hub
cards.subtitle: Avery Hall
cards.notes: Study among towering bookshelves and classic wooden furniture. The main floor offers a quiet, removed atmosphere perfect for arts and humanities students.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library known for its collegiate aesthetic and quiet communal tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Avery Library's main floor features long coworking tables and is a quiet study space removed from the real world.
cards.access_notes: Check library website for seasonal hours; CUID required.

cards.title: The Modern Glass Box
cards.subtitle: Northwest Corner Building
cards.notes: Utilize this bright, modern space for collaborative work. The floor-to-ceiling windows provide ample natural light and views of the Upper West Side.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary, light-filled library focused on science and engineering research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science & Engineering Library in the Northwest Corner Building provides a collaborative environment with modern seating.
cards.access_notes: CUID required; group study rooms can be reserved online.

cards.title: The Collaborative Zone
cards.subtitle: Uris Hall
cards.notes: Head here if you prefer a low buzz of conversation while you work. It is one of the few campus libraries where talking and eating are generally permitted.
cards.short_summary: A business-focused library that encourages group work and active discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watson Library is the only library where talking and eating is generally allowed due to the collaborative nature of assignments.
cards.access_notes: Undergraduate access may be restricted during peak finals periods.

cards.title: The Green Chair View
cards.subtitle: Barnard College
cards.notes: Snag a signature green chair facing the floor-to-ceiling windows. This floor offers a mix of individual carrels and open collaborative areas.
cards.short_summary: A popular study floor at Barnard featuring natural light and varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of the Milstein Center is known for its green chairs and floor-to-ceiling windows that fill the space with sunlight.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season
cards.access_notes: Open to both Barnard and Columbia students with valid ID.

cards.title: The Global Affairs Nook
cards.subtitle: International Affairs Building
cards.notes: Work in this spacious library located within the SIPA building. It is excellent for group projects, with several reservable rooms and large tables.
cards.short_summary: A large library in the SIPA building housing social science and map collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehman Social Sciences Library offers group study rooms and a collaborative environment for students.
cards.access_notes: CUID required; located on the 300 level of the IAB.

cards.title: The Quiet Retreat
cards.subtitle: Teachers College, Russell Hall
cards.notes: Climb to the third floor for a strictly quiet study experience. The space is scenic and less frequented by undergraduates from the main campus.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, intensive study space located within the Teachers College library.
cards.evidence_claim: The 3rd floor of the Gottesman Library is a quiet space recommended for intensive study time.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study On Campus!
cards.access_notes: Accessible to Columbia students; check TC-specific hours.

cards.title: The High-Energy Cafe
cards.subtitle: Northwest Corner Building, Lobby
cards.notes: Join the bustle at this popular cafe. It is a prime spot for those who study best with background noise and easy access to caffeine.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant campus cafe with ample seating and a modern aesthetic.
cards.evidence_claim: Joe Coffee in the NoCo building is a classic campus spot where people stay and study for hours.
cards.source_title: Columbia University Northwest Corner Building - Joe Coffee Company
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; seating is first-come, first-served.

cards.title: The Cubicle Corner
cards.subtitle: The Diana Center
cards.notes: Use the desk cubicles on this floor for a sense of privacy. The large windows provide natural light without the heavy traffic of the main libraries.
cards.short_summary: A quieter study area in the Diana Center featuring individual work stations.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of the Diana Center has a room filled with desk cubicles and large windows for natural light.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season
cards.access_notes: Open to Barnard and Columbia students.

cards.title: The Grad Student Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: 302 Philosophy Hall
cards.notes: Reserve this room for student-driven initiatives or quiet study. It is specifically reserved for graduate students, offering a more mature environment.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated seminar and study room for graduate students in Philosophy Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Seminar Room in 302 Philosophy Hall is available to graduate students with valid CUIDs.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students only; booking required for groups.

boards.school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Columbia's Morningside Heights and Manhattanville campuses, from the historic 'Frat Row' to the modern developments of 125th Street.

cards.title: The Main Commercial Strip
cards.subtitle: Broadway Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this stretch to find student staples like Tom's Restaurant and Book Culture. It serves as the primary retail and dining artery for the Morningside Heights community.
cards.short_summary: The primary commercial corridor for Columbia students, featuring historic diners, bookstores, and essential retail.
cards.evidence_claim: Broadway and Amsterdam Avenue are the main commercial streets in the area, offering a variety of food markets, restaurants, shops and bookstores.
cards.access_notes: Public city street with 24/7 sidewalk access; business hours vary by establishment.

cards.title: The Cathedral District
cards.subtitle: Amsterdam Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Hungarian Pastry Shop for a study session across from the Cathedral of St. John the Divine. This area offers a quieter, more scenic alternative to Broadway.
cards.short_summary: A scenic stretch of Amsterdam Avenue home to the world's largest cathedral and popular student study cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cathedral of Saint John the Divine is located a few blocks away from campus between 113th and 110th Street, across from the popular Hungarian Pastry Shop.
cards.source_title: A guide to Morningside Heights as a Columbia student
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; the Cathedral grounds are generally open to the public during daylight hours.

cards.title: Historic Frat Row
cards.subtitle: West 114th Street
cards.notes: Pass by the historic brownstones housing Columbia's Greek life. This residential block is a hub for student social activity and sits directly south of Butler Library.
cards.short_summary: Known as 'Frat Row,' this block features many of the university's fraternity and sorority brownstones.
cards.evidence_claim: Frat Row is the stretch of 114th St between Broadway and Amsterdam where a lot of fraternities and sororities are located.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; brownstone interiors are restricted to residents and invited guests.

cards.title: The Manhattanville Gateway
cards.subtitle: 125th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the new Manhattanville campus expansion, featuring the Jerome L. Greene Science Center and the Forum. It connects the university to the heart of West Harlem.
cards.short_summary: The northern anchor of Columbia's expansion, featuring modern architecture and public community spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Manhattanville campus spans 17 acres from 125th Street to 134th Street between Broadway and 12th Avenue.
cards.source_title: Manhattanville campus construction continues into its 17th year
cards.access_notes: Public street; university buildings like The Forum have public-access ground floors.

cards.title: The Eastern Overlook
cards.subtitle: Morningside Drive Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along the stone wall for panoramic views of Morningside Park and Harlem. This quiet street borders the eastern edge of the Morningside Heights campus.
cards.short_summary: A scenic residential street offering elevated views of the park and the city skyline to the east.
cards.evidence_claim: Morningside Drive is the eastern boundary of Morningside Heights, overlooking Morningside Park built on a steep incline.
cards.access_notes: Public street and sidewalk; best visited during daylight for park views.

cards.title: The Residential Hub
cards.subtitle: West 113th Street
cards.notes: Find several large residence halls like 600 W 113th (Nussbaum) and McBain Hall. This block is densely populated by sophomores and juniors.
cards.short_summary: A key residential block for upperclassmen, housing several large university-owned dormitories.
cards.evidence_claim: 600 West 113th Street (Nussbaum) is a residence hall housing a mix of sophomores, juniors, and seniors.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; dorm access requires CUID swipe.

cards.title: The Western Parkside
cards.subtitle: Riverside Drive Corridor
cards.notes: Head west to this scenic drive to access Riverside Park's running paths and sunset views. It marks the western boundary of the university's neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A grand residential avenue bordering Riverside Park, popular for recreation and quiet walks.
cards.evidence_claim: Morningside Heights is bounded by Riverside Drive to the west, providing access to Riverside Park.
cards.access_notes: Public street and park access; park is open daily from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: The Manhattanville Connector
cards.subtitle: LaSalle Street
cards.notes: Walk this street to see the transition between Morningside Heights and the Manhattanville campus. It houses several graduate student residences.
cards.short_summary: A short street in the northern part of the neighborhood housing several Columbia Residential buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Columbia Residential buildings like 100 LaSalle and 124 LaSalle are located in the Morningside Heights and Manhattanville area.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street.

cards.title: The Quiet Residential Block
cards.subtitle: West 115th Street
cards.notes: Stroll past brownstones and dorms like 627 W 115th. This block offers a more residential feel just steps away from the main campus gates.
cards.short_summary: A primarily residential street housing several university-owned apartment buildings and dorms.
cards.evidence_claim: 627 W. 115th Street is a residence hall typically housing seniors and juniors.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street.

cards.title: The Institutional Corridor
cards.subtitle: Amsterdam Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Observe the Law School and School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) buildings. The Law Bridge spans this avenue, connecting the main campus to East Campus.
cards.short_summary: A stretch of Amsterdam Avenue dominated by university academic buildings and the Law Bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: Amsterdam Avenue is mostly lined by institutional buildings owned by Columbia, as well as St. Luke's Hospital.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; the Law Bridge is accessible to CUID holders.

boards.school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From satirical musicals to midnight screams, these traditions define the unique academic and social rhythm of Columbia University.

cards.title: The Varsity Show
cards.subtitle: Columbia's Oldest Performing Arts Tradition
cards.notes: Attend this student-written musical satire that skewers campus life and administrators. It has run since 1894 and counts Richard Rodgers and Kate McKinnon as alumni.
cards.short_summary: An annual satirical musical production written and performed by students to poke fun at Columbia life.
cards.evidence_claim: The Varsity Show is Columbia's oldest performing arts tradition, founded in 1894, and is written, directed, and performed entirely by undergraduate students.
cards.access_notes: Performances typically occur in April at Roone Arledge Auditorium in Lerner Hall.

cards.title: Tree Lighting Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Illuminating College Walk
cards.notes: Join the countdown on College Walk as the trees are illuminated for the winter. Enjoy hot chocolate and a cappella performances during this late-semester gathering.
cards.short_summary: An annual winter event where the trees lining College Walk are lit simultaneously following a community countdown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tree Lighting Ceremony began in 1998 and features a countdown to the illumination of trees along College Walk, accompanied by music and refreshments.
cards.source_title: What Does It Take to Start a Tradition? | Columbia College Today
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December on College Walk.

cards.title: Finding the Hidden Owl
cards.subtitle: A Superstition of Wisdom
cards.notes: Look for the small owl hidden in the folds of the Alma Mater statue's robes. Legend says the first student to find it will become valedictorian.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition involving a hidden owl on the Alma Mater statue that supposedly predicts academic success.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alma Mater statue features a hidden owl in its robes, which has inspired legends including the belief that the first student to find it will be valedictorian.
cards.source_title: Lore and Pranks - Columbia University Libraries
cards.access_notes: The statue is located on the steps of Low Memorial Library and is accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Primal Scream
cards.subtitle: Midnight Finals Stress Relief
cards.notes: Open your window or head to Butler Library at midnight on the Sunday before finals to join a collective, cathartic scream to release academic pressure.
cards.short_summary: A biannual tradition where students scream at midnight during finals week to relieve stress.
cards.evidence_claim: Primal Scream is an end-of-semester tradition where students release stress by howling at midnight before the start of final exams.
cards.source_title: Biannual 'primal scream' tradition morphs into pro-Palestinian rally - Columbia Spectator
cards.access_notes: Occurs at midnight on the Sunday before finals week; traditionally centered around Butler Library.

cards.title: Yule Log Ceremony
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Holiday Ritual
cards.notes: Watch students in colonial attire carry a Yule Log into John Jay Hall. This tradition dates back to 1910 and includes seasonal carols and readings.
cards.short_summary: One of Columbia's oldest traditions, involving the ceremonial carrying of a Yule Log to a fireplace in John Jay Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Yule Log ceremony was established in 1910 by President Nicholas Murray Butler and involves students in colonial costumes ushering the log to the John Jay Hall fireplace.
cards.source_title: The Yule Log Tradition Is More Than 100 Years Old | Columbia College Today
cards.access_notes: Held in John Jay Hall lounge following the Tree Lighting Ceremony in December.

cards.title: Bacchanal
cards.subtitle: The Annual Spring Concert
cards.notes: Experience Columbia's largest music festival on the Low Steps. Past headliners have included major artists like Snoop Dogg and Vampire Weekend.
cards.short_summary: A major annual spring music festival featuring professional headliners and student performers on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Bacchanal is Columbia's premier annual spring concert, featuring professional artists and student acts, typically held on the steps of Low Library.
cards.access_notes: Tickets are free but required for undergraduate students; usually held in April.

cards.title: Surf & Turf Night
cards.subtitle: A Dining Hall Feast
cards.notes: Use a meal swipe for a special end-of-year dinner featuring steak and lobster. This annual event transforms the dining halls into a festive celebration.
cards.short_summary: An annual high-end meal event in the dining halls featuring steak and lobster for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Surf & Turf is an annual springtime event hosted by Columbia Dining featuring steak, lobster, and shrimp at John Jay and Ferris Booth Commons.
cards.access_notes: Requires a meal swipe or dining hall entry fee; typically held in late April.

cards.title: Class Day Pinning
cards.subtitle: Connecting Generations of Alumni
cards.notes: Receive a class pin from a member of the 50th reunion class during your graduation ceremony. It’s a symbolic welcome into the alumni community.
cards.short_summary: A graduation tradition where seniors receive pins from alumni who graduated 50 years prior.
cards.evidence_claim: During Class Day, undergraduate students receive a Class Pin from members of the 50th reunion class of that year.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the respective Class Day ceremonies for Columbia College and SEAS on South Lawn.

cards.title: Orgo Night
cards.subtitle: The Band's Midnight Performance
cards.notes: Witness the Marching Band's satirical performance on the eve of the Organic Chemistry exam. Though its location has shifted, the humor remains a finals staple.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing satirical performance by the marching band held at midnight before the first day of finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Orgo Night is held at midnight on the day before the Organic Chemistry exam, featuring the marching band playing music and telling jokes.
cards.access_notes: Traditionally held in Butler Library Room 209, though recent years have seen outdoor or alternative locations.

cards.title: First-Year March
cards.subtitle: Entering the Gates
cards.notes: Walk through the main gates on 116th Street as a new student during orientation. This ceremonial entry marks your official start as a member of the Columbia community.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial march through the campus gates for incoming freshmen during orientation week.
cards.evidence_claim: During the First Year March, students enter campus through the main gates while being serenaded by staff to officially become Columbia students.
cards.access_notes: Takes place during New Student Orientation Program (NSOP) in late August.

boards.school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
boards.title: Your First Weekend at Columbia University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Attend the Convocation Ceremony
cards.subtitle: The formal start of your Columbia journey
cards.notes: Gather on the steps of Low Plaza for the official welcome ceremony. This event marks your transition into the undergraduate community alongside fellow first-year students.
cards.short_summary: The official welcome ceremony for new students held outdoors on the iconic Low Plaza steps.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2026 Convocation ceremony will be held on August 30, 2026, on Low Plaza, following move-in and check-in activities.
cards.source_title: First-Year Students | Columbia College and Columbia Engineering
cards.access_notes: Open to all incoming first-year students and their families during orientation week.

cards.title: Grab Your First Campus Meal
cards.subtitle: A classic first-year dining experience
cards.notes: Visit the first floor of John Jay Hall for a buffet-style meal. It is a central hub for first-year students to meet and eat during their first weekend on campus.
cards.short_summary: A primary undergraduate dining hall offering continuous food service and a variety of stations.
cards.evidence_claim: John Jay Dining Hall is located on the first floor of John Jay Hall and offers continuous service during operational hours.
cards.source_title: John Jay Dining Hall | Columbia Dining
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid CUID and a dining plan or guest pass for entry.

cards.title: Pick Up Your Blue and White Gear
cards.subtitle: Located in the lower level of Lerner Hall
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of the student center to stock up on Columbia-branded apparel and essential school supplies before classes begin on Monday.
cards.short_summary: The official university bookstore selling textbooks, school supplies, and emblematic apparel.
cards.evidence_claim: The Columbia University Bookstore is located on the lower level of Lerner Hall and is open 11:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m. on weekends.
cards.source_title: Departments and Hours : First Floor - Alfred J. Lerner Hall
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; accessible via the first floor of Lerner Hall.

cards.title: Explore the Milstein Undergraduate Library
cards.subtitle: Your 24-hour study destination
cards.notes: Walk through the stacks of Butler Library to find your future study spot. The Milstein floors offer 24-hour access to resources for undergraduate students.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library featuring the Philip L. Milstein Family College Library for undergraduates.
cards.evidence_claim: The Philip L. Milstein Family College Library provides 24-hour access to resources on the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th floors of Butler Library.
cards.source_title: Milstein Undergraduate Library & Services | Columbia University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid CUID for entry; 24-hour access is standard during the academic year.

cards.title: Find the Hidden Owl
cards.subtitle: A legendary campus tradition
cards.notes: Search the folds of the Alma Mater statue's robes to find the hidden owl. Legend says the first student to find it will become the class valedictorian.
cards.short_summary: A student tradition involving finding a hidden owl on the iconic Alma Mater statue in Low Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: Legend holds that the first member of the incoming class to find the owl hidden on the statue of Alma Mater will become the class valedictorian.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors on Low Plaza; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Activate Your Gym Membership
cards.subtitle: Complimentary access for undergraduates
cards.notes: Visit the tri-level fitness area to check out the equipment and indoor track. Your CUID provides complimentary access to these facilities.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus fitness facility offering cardio, weights, a pool, and an indoor track.
cards.evidence_claim: All students from Columbia College and SEAS have complimentary access to Dodge Fitness Center with their Columbia ID.
cards.source_title: An introduction to Dodge Fitness Center - Columbia Spectator
cards.access_notes: Open 8:00 a.m. - 8:00 p.m. on weekends; requires CUID for entry.

cards.title: Walk Along the Hudson River
cards.subtitle: A scenic escape just blocks from campus
cards.notes: Take a short walk west to Riverside Park for views of the Hudson River. It is a popular spot for students to jog, read, or watch the sunset.
cards.short_summary: A historic waterfront park located on the Upper West Side, easily accessible from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Riverside Park is located on the West side of the Morningside Heights neighborhood and is a popular place for the student population.
cards.source_title: NYC Walk: Columbia University & Morningside Heights
cards.access_notes: Public park; open daily from 6:00 a.m. to 1:00 a.m.

cards.title: Visit the Historic Landmark
cards.subtitle: A multi-faith venue on campus
cards.notes: Step inside this historic landmark to appreciate its architecture or attend a multi-faith service. It serves as a quiet space for reflection.
cards.short_summary: A historic multi-faith chapel on campus hosting religious services and concerts.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Paul's Chapel is one of the first buildings in New York City to be designated as an official historic landmark and serves as a multi-faith venue.
cards.access_notes: Typically open Monday-Friday 9am-5pm; check for weekend event schedules.

cards.title: Study at a Neighborhood Landmark
cards.subtitle: A favorite off-campus coffee spot
cards.notes: Visit this cozy bakery across from the Cathedral of St. John the Divine. It is a legendary spot for students to write and enjoy coffee with free refills.
cards.short_summary: A historic neighborhood bakery and coffee shop popular with Columbia students and writers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hungarian Pastry Shop is a very popular spot for Columbia students looking for a coffee shop to study in near campus.
cards.source_title: A guide to Morningside Heights as a Columbia student
cards.access_notes: Open daily; often has a line on weekends. No Wi-Fi policy encourages focused work.

cards.title: Join the Saturday Night Social
cards.subtitle: Meet your classmates in a relaxed setting
cards.notes: Cap off your first Saturday with a social event like Karaoke Night. These late-night activities are designed to help you bond with your new cohort.
cards.short_summary: A social event held during orientation week to facilitate community building among new students.
cards.evidence_claim: Karaoke Night is a scheduled NSOP event where new students can perform in a casual, relaxed setting.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to new students participating in the NSOP program.
